ch37.d.beta: Relative speed of the two frames, $\beta = v/c$
ch37.assume.units: Units: $c = 1$; lengths in light-seconds (ls, the distance light travels in 1 s), times in s
ch37.c.goal.dilate: A moving clock runs slow: $\Delta t = \gamma\,\Delta t_0$
ch37.c.goal.mutual: The effect is mutual: in each frame the other frame's clock runs slow
ch37.c.obs.zigzag: Moving light clock: the light runs a slanted zigzag at the same speed $c$, so each round trip takes longer
ch37.c.obs.count: The number on a clock counts its round trips (ticks); the clock at rest counts faster
ch37.c.obs.both: From S the S′ clock is slow; from S′ the S clock is slow. Neither frame is special
ch37.c.assume.clock: Mirrors 1 ls apart, so a clock at rest ticks every $\Delta t_0$ = 2 s. A moving clock that leaves the view comes back on the other side
ch37.l.goal.contract: A moving rod is shorter along its motion: $L = L_0/\gamma$
ch37.l.goal.mutual: The proper length $L_0$ is measured in the rod's rest frame; the effect is mutual
ch37.l.obs.short: The rod's tick marks shrink by the same factor
ch37.l.obs.both: From S the S′ rod is short; from S′ the S rod is short
ch37.l.obs.beta: Lengths across the motion (the rod's thickness) do not change
ch37.l.assume.rod: Both rods have proper length 4 ls, marks every 1 ls of proper length
ch37.d.d.grid: S grid (grey) and S′ grid (orange, lines of constant $x'$ and $ct'$)
ch37.d.goal.axes: The S′ axes look tilted in S: the $ct'$ axis has slope $1/\beta$, the $x'$ axis slope $\beta$, symmetric about the light path (45°)
ch37.d.goal.simul: Lines of simultaneity (events at the same time) differ between frames
ch37.d.obs.drag: Drag events A and B; the table at the top left gives their coordinates in both frames
ch37.d.obs.simul: Default: A and B are simultaneous in S (one blue dashed line), but in S′ B comes first ($\Delta t' < 0$)
ch37.d.obs.order: Events outside each other's light cone can change order between frames; inside it, the order is fixed
ch37.d.obs.light: The light cone (grey dashed) is the same in both frames: light moves at $c$ in every inertial frame
ch37.d.assume.origin: The origins coincide ($t = t' = 0$ at $x = x' = 0$)
ch37.s.goal.relative: Two events simultaneous in one frame are not simultaneous in another
ch37.s.goal.c: Light moves at $c$ in both frames, which is why the arrival times differ
ch37.s.obs.train: Train frame (bottom): the flash starts at the centre and reaches both ends at the same time
ch37.s.obs.ground: Ground frame (top): the rear end moves toward the light and the front end away from it, so the rear is reached first
ch37.s.obs.dt: The ground-frame time difference is $\Delta t = \gamma v L_0/c^2$, larger for larger β
ch37.s.obs.diagram: Plot the two arrival events on the spacetime diagram tab for the same result
ch37.s.assume.train: Train proper length 4 ls; the flash goes off at the centre ($x = x' = 0$) at $t = t' = 0$; the light is absorbed at the ends
